title.narrative: OHCHR - UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine - III (2025-2027)
OHCHR - UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine - III (2025-2027)

description.narrative:
Syftet med insatsen är att förbättra mänskliga rättigheter (MR) i Ukraina, och då särskilt dokumentering av våld och övergrepp som sker som konsekvens av Rysslands fullskaliga invasion samt i de delar som sedan 2014 ockuperats av Ryssland.
Insatsen syftar till att öka medvetenheten kring människorättskränkningar bland relevanta ukrainska och internationella aktörer, samt stärka deras kapacitet att identifiera och reagera på kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna.

The aim of the intervention is to improve human rights in Ukraine, in particular monitoring and documentation of violence and violations taking place as a consequence of Russia's full scale invasion and the area under Russian occupation since 2014.
The intervention aims at increased awareness of human rights violations among relevant Ukrainian and international actors and strengthen their capacity to identify and react to human rights violations. Among other things, then intervention aims to monitor gender-related human rights violations, produce topic-specific and periodic reports, including conflict-related sexual violence, gender equality with actionable recommendations to alleviate the impact of conflict, inequality, discrimination as well as advocate for a more enabling environment and policy level recommendations.

The goal of HRMMU is: Increased respect and protection of human rights of women, men, girls and boys across all of Ukraine, including territory occupied by the Russian Federation, enabled by HRMMUs monitoring, reporting, advocacy, and engagement with national and international duty bearers.

During 2026 (Jan-July), HRMMU produced eight monthly reports on protection of civilians in armed conflict, as well as four thematic and other reports capturing the extent of the human rights violations by Russia in Ukraine. The findings in these reports have been utilised by other UN entities, Ukrainian government and civil society actors as well as donors to inform decision-making and raise awareness based on verified and acknowledged impartial evidence. Media and news outlets are using the data and findings of HRMMU in their reporting.
Since the beginning of the full scale invasion, HRMMU has documented 68,000 civilian casualties. From January to July 2026, HRMMU documented, verified and reported over ten thousand injured and eighteen hundred killed civilians by Russian attacks, an increase of 70 per cent compared to the July 2025. July 2026 was the month with the highest number of civilian causalities since March 2022. In July 2026, long-range weapons were noted as the leading cause of casualties (38 per cent of total), while short-range drones near the frontline reached their highest monthly level and caused 27 per cent of all casualties. HRMMU also noted an increase between June (12) and July (31) in Ukrainian attacks on energy systems in Russian occupied Crimea; while Russia continued their continuous attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
